issues.legal_issue: An appeal cannot be heard and decided after a respondent whose estate must be represented has died until the court determines and brings the legal representative or representatives on record.
material_facts: A successful plaintiff died while the defendant's appeal from the decree was pending, and the right to continue the case survived against her estate.
Her husband and her nieces and nephews each sought to represent her estate, and the dispute between them remained undecided when the High Court heard and allowed the appeal.
The husband was added as legal representative only after the High Court had delivered its judgment.
issues.conclusion: The High Court could not proceed to hear the appeal on the merits before determining who represented the deceased respondent's estate and bringing that person or those persons on record. Because the estate remained unrepresented when the appeal was decided, the High Court's judgment was a nullity and inoperative; the appeal was restored for the High Court to determine representation first and then hear it on the merits.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(11) of the Code of Civil Procedure defines a legal representative to include a person who represents the estate or intermeddles with it. Order 22 Rules 4 and 5, read with Rule 11, require determination of a disputed representative and the bringing of the representative on record before an appeal can proceed. Section 33, Order 20 Rule 1, and Order 41 Rule 30 support the principle that judgment follows a hearing; an appeal is not heard in the eye of law when the deceased respondent's estate is unrepresented.

rule.if: appeal_from_a_decree and respondent_dies_during_appeal and right_to_continue_survives_against_estate and estate_unrepresented_when_appeal_decided

predicates.appeal_from_a_decree: The proceeding is an appeal from a decree.
predicates.respondent_dies_during_appeal: A respondent dies while the appeal is pending.
predicates.right_to_continue_survives_against_estat: The right to continue the proceeding survives against the deceased respondent's estate.
predicates.estate_unrepresented_when_appeal_decided: The appeal is decided before a legal representative has been determined and brought on record to represent the deceased respondent's estate.

issues.definition: When a respondent dies during an appeal from a decree, the right to continue survives against the estate, and that estate remains unrepresented when the appeal is decided, the appellate judgment is a nullity.

issues.legal_issue: A determination of who represents a deceased party's estate in a pending case is limited to representation in that case and does not determine entitlement to the estate's property.
material_facts: The deceased respondent's husband claimed to be her sole heir, while her nieces and nephews claimed that wills made them beneficiaries of the suit property and sought to represent her estate.
The High Court considered the competing claims in connection with the pending appeal and purported to determine who should be substituted.
issues.conclusion: A determination of legal representation is only for representing the deceased's estate in the case being adjudicated; it confers no right to the property in dispute against rival claimants and does not decide their rights in independent proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 22 Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the court determines who is the legal representative for the limited purpose of representation of the deceased's estate in that case. That determination does not adjudicate ownership or confer rights to the property that is the subject matter of the suit.

predicates.pending_case_requires_estate_representat: A pending case requires someone to represent the estate of a deceased party.
predicates.competing_claims_to_estate_representatio: Different claimants dispute who should represent the deceased party's estate in that case.

issues.definition: When a pending case requires estate representation and claimants dispute who should provide it, the determination identifies representation for that case only.

issues.legal_issue: A legatee who intends to represent a deceased person's estate may qualify as that person's legal representative by intermeddling with the estate.
material_facts: The deceased's nieces and nephews claimed that she had bequeathed the suit property to them and sought to come on record to represent her estate.
The competing claimants disputed whether the nieces and nephews or the deceased's husband should represent the estate.
issues.conclusion: A legatee who intends to represent the deceased testator's estate is an intermeddler and may be a legal representative, subject to the court determining the representation question.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(11) of the Code of Civil Procedure includes within the definition of legal representative a person who intermeddles with the deceased's estate. A legatee intending to represent the testator's estate falls within that definition.

predicates.deceased_party_in_pending_case: A party to a pending case has died and the estate requires representation.
predicates.legatee_intends_to_represent_estate: A person claiming a legacy intends to represent the deceased person's estate in the pending case.

issues.definition: When a party to a pending case has died and a legatee intends to represent the estate, the legatee may qualify as a legal representative.
